items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: with the Lonnie Polk band - Yeah, mostly, yeah

ctx.x: And you adopt, get adapted to some of those sounds that you hear, automatically without even rehearsing or practicing or trying things out. But then, there, it was nobody to listen to, you had to play with your - so anybody can play, improvise if they know the harmony. See, you don't have to have no guide, you just play the harmony. If a chord is a C seven and you just practicin', use a C seven in different ways. And it may not sound like that person or that person but it will be correct, see what I mean?

Of the other bands you were playing with in Philadelphia around this period - first of all, when Driver heard you and recommended you to Charlie Miller, was that a gig with Lonnie Polk or was that just -

No, that was different, that was a gig with a, it was a dance band, I was working at the Waltz Dream - did I say Waltz Dream before? - yeah, Waltz Dream, it was a dancing hall for negroes. Lot of people would be there, see - I think it was three times a week or something like that. And we had music - see, you could buy, you could buy stock arrangements, that's when the birth of stock arrangements, you know. And you also buy semi-swing things, you know, little things by guys like, have you ever heard of a guy…
